tidy_items: when the division guess is wrong, the _len fallback `sum(1 for _ in self)` counts every item, which is O(n) and is computed at construction time. A large float range whose guess is off by one could take a very long time to build. It should adjust the guess by +/-1 instead, and the issue itself promised to keep current performance
tests are in a new file tests/test_numeric_range_float_consistency.py instead of tests/test_more.py
the tests use exception-to-AssertionError wrappers
G07.reason: len, `in`, index and count are all now decided against the items start + n*step that iteration actually produces: a checked fast path, then a binary search. Exact types keep their exact answers. However, the full-iteration fallback in _len is a real performance flaw that has to be fixed before applying.
